claim: Carrying the CNS state across tokens (persist) lowers held-out loss on temporal-memory tasks compared with resetting it every token, for a real-wiring core with learned Dale-preserving edges.

protocol.notes: 3,000-type subgraph (synapse-mass core + proportional inputs/outputs; 629,875 edges): the per-token persistent scan costs ~4x a reset step, which the full graph cannot afford here. 2 of every 8 rows are synthetic temporal-memory rows (recall at a distance, pattern, count, first item) in every arm.

notes: Both arms: 4 microsteps per token, same subgraph, same rows (incl. temporal rows). The trunk's attention already sees the whole prompt, so the question is whether a recurrent CNS state adds anything on top of it.
